query: How active is the 2026 US tornado season and what is the forecast/outlook for early July 2026 severe weather? Current ENSO state (La Nina/El Nino) for summer 2026 and any Climate Prediction Center outlook for July 2026 severe convective weather in northern Plains and Midwest.
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Summary

**2026 tornado season — ACTIVE, above-average pace:**
- ~1,164 preliminary tornado reports through July 2, 2026 (1,100+ through late June); 78 deaths
- After a below-average spring, **June 2026 became the most active June since 1998** (390 reports), pushing the season above the climatological mean
- Notable: May 19–26 super outbreak (162 tornadoes in 24 hrs, 2nd largest single-day ever), 3rd most active March on record, and two rare EF5s (Indiana; Minnesota's first-ever EF5)
- **Illinois has led the nation** all year — a marked eastward shift of activity into the Midwest/Dixie Alley

**Early July 2026 severe weather:**
- Current SPC Day 1 (July 17): Marginal Risk over Upper Midwest/Great Lakes and northern Rockies, with a brief tornado threat in N. Minnesota/Wisconsin/Michigan UP
- Earlier July featured Enhanced Risks: July 1 (Upper Midwest/Great Lakes) and July 14 (Northeast)

**ENSO state — IMPORTANT CORRECTION:** Summer 2026 is **El Niño, NOT La Niña.** An El Niño Advisory is in effect (moderate strength, strengthening; Niño-3.4 at +1.2 to +1.3°C), forecast to intensify to a ~81% chance of a *very strong* El Niño by Oct–Dec 2026.

**CPC outlook (northern Plains/Midwest):** CPC's late-July hazards outlook flags **above-normal temperatures and Rapid Onset Drought risk in the Northern Plains** plus extreme heat over the south-central US — a heat/subsidence pattern that tends to suppress local severe convection, keeping the active corridor focused farther east. (Note: CPC doesn't issue month-long severe convective outlooks — that's SPC's Day 1–8 domain.)

Full structured findings with all data points and sources have been submitted.

key_facts: 2026 US tornado count reached ~1,164 preliminary reports through July 2, 2026 (1,100+ through late June), running ABOVE the historical mean pace with 78 deaths.
June 2026 was the most active June since 1998, with 390 preliminary tornado reports — the main driver of the season surging above average after a below-average spring.
The May 19–26, 2026 super outbreak produced 162 tornadoes in 24 hours, the 2nd largest single-day count ever recorded.
Two EF5 tornadoes occurred in 2026: Wells County, Indiana (March 10) and Minnesota (May outbreak, first EF5 in Minnesota history).
Illinois led the nation in tornado counts for most of 2026 (~170+ confirmed, surpassing its record year), reflecting an eastward shift of activity into the Midwest/Dixie Alley.
Summer 2026 ENSO state is EL NIÑO (not La Niña): El Niño Advisory in effect, moderate strength, strengthening.
Latest weekly Niño-3.4 index was +1.2°C (CPC ENSO discussion) to +1.3°C (CPC 30-day discussion, July 16, 2026).
El Niño is forecast to intensify: ~81% chance of very strong El Niño in Oct–Dec 2026 and ~97% chance it continues into early spring 2027.

SPC Day 1 outlook for July 17, 2026 was a Marginal Risk (level 1/5) including the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes and northern Rockies, with a brief tornado threat in northern Minnesota/Wisconsin/Michigan UP.
Earlier July 2026 featured Enhanced Risks (level 3/5): July 1 (Upper Midwest/Great Lakes, ~80 mph gusts) and July 14 (Northeast, strong tornado potential).
CPC Probabilistic Hazards Outlook (valid July 24–30, 2026) flags above-normal Northern Plains temperatures with continued Rapid Onset Drought risk and extreme heat over south-central CONUS.
March 2026 was the 3rd most active March on record with 204 tornadoes.
